title: Information first, decoration never.
text: An element earns pixels by telling the reader something. Initial avatars, doc thumbnails, row glyphs, FAB, Share: cut. A real author photo is information; an initial is not.

title: Complete identifiers, never truncated.
text: PR titles wrap, never ellipsise. Repo + number always scannable. Branch means both ends: head → base. Diffstat always coloured.

title: Dense but calm meta.
text: All the facts (number, author, diffstat, checks, age) but never one cluttered line. Group, align, give variable fields fixed width.

title: Lists are the backbone.
text: Rows grouped by repo, chips for scope. Tappable rows look tappable (chevron, pressed state). Swipe actions are the fast path. No explanatory copy or empty-state prose under a populated list.

title: Sheets over the page, not new pages.
text: Bottom sheets for grouped actions, chat, composer, files. Dim everything beneath, uniformly, including the header and the trigger.

title: Words mean what they do.
text: Sections, not stops. Buttons name their effect. Cites say where they lead and are tappable. Every paragraph is labelled (Summary / Description).

title: Irreversible actions are never primary.
text: Merge lives behind the ⋯ menu. The bottom primary is the reviewing action (Review 4 files, Next).

title: No cards for numbers.
text: Stat tiles / KPI cards are ugly. No boxed mini-widgets; typographic hierarchy on a flat page.

title: The diff is the product.
text: Full-width lines, hunk expanders, word highlights, line numbers. Add/remove backgrounds clearly visible. Inline thread cards on their line. Files via a drawer or menu plus ‹ ›, never snapped tabs or horizontal swipe.

title: Composer: two modes.
text: Comment and Ask Pulls only. Split visual layout, not three text chips. No counters, no voice.

title: Not wanted, ever.
text: Voice/dictation. Suggestion mode. Share on PR/tour. “Up next” inside a tour. FAB with unclear scope. “Later” as a row action. Numbered step pips. Tiny provenance labels. Step counters in progress states.

title: Scale and tone.
text: 26px+ plain PR title (no chat bubble). Perplexity palette: warm off-white, teal accent, deep ink. Generous element size.

title: Alignment first.
text: Number, author, age, diffstat sit in fixed columns so every row lines up. Test: add a digit, swap a longer author name. Nothing else may move. Misalignment is the first thing he sees.

title: No tiny grey text.
text: Small uppercase labels, eyebrows, provenance lines, counters (“1 of 4 reviewed”, “Section 3 of 7”) are awful. Body-size ink or nothing. Never below 15px, never uppercase-tracked. A section label is one word: Summary.

title: One row anatomy everywhere.
text: A PR row is identical in Inbox, Tours, search: title, number, author, coloured diffstat, checks, age. Context-free counts (“7 sections”) never replace them.

title: Status words only where they vary.
text: A group titled “Ready to read” does not repeat Ready on each row. Failing / passing get a real icon, not a dot.

title: Swipe commits, tap opens.
text: Swipe left archives, swipe right opens the review, as full Mail-style gestures. No reveal-then-tap. Blur the displaced row content slightly. Keep clearance from anything revealed.

title: AI work looks alive.
text: In-progress analysis is a live, animated thinking indicator that feels smart. Never show the internal step. Make it tappable.

title: Analyze is one action, three outputs.
text: Analysing a PR = summary + per-file explanations + tour. Call it Analyze, not Write tour. An unanalysed PR is a real state with a visible way in. Per-file explanations show on the file rows.

title: Summary and Description, both first-class.
text: Description = what the author wrote. Summary = what the AI produced. One easy switch on the PR page.

title: Identifiers look like GitHub's.
text: Branches are squarish pills, head → base, tap to copy. Cites keep the concept but drop mono and the current pill style; try Mona Sans.

title: Counts: neither cards nor a run-on sentence.
text: No stat tiles, and no “+180 −32 across 4 files · 2 commits · 2 checks failing · 0 of 4 reviewed” either. Aligned label/value columns where nothing moves when digits change.

title: Sub-pages keep their context.
text: A tour section page carries the PR title and number in its header, with progress as a small element there. No pips, no eyebrow, no bottom “X of Y”.

title: Buttons are one line.
text: “Next unreviewed” becomes “Next”. A wrapped label is a defect.

title: Nothing overflows the frame.
text: No horizontal scroll, no scrollbar, nothing inside the 16px margin. Sliding rows clip inside the frame. Render at 390×844 before publishing.

title: Meta lines are one line.
text: Author · repo #number · age on one line; head → base on one line. Each segment ellipsises, nothing wraps.

title: Icons, not words, for segment navigation.
text: Overview / Changes / Tour is three icons in a capsule. Words are for tabs inside a page.

title: Summary / Description are underline tabs.
text: Pills are spent on chips, branches and cites.

title: The ⋯ sheet is on every PR screen.
text: Checks, GitHub, Analyze again; Approve, Request changes, Squash and merge, Merge when checks pass, Convert to draft, Close. Reachable from the PR, diff and tour headers.

title: Ask is a quiet toolbar.
text: “✦ Ask | ⋯” in a floating capsule beside the primary button. Never a second Ask inside a comment card. A sparkle alone is not a label: AI actions get a word or a real icon.

title: Tour sections scroll.
text: One scrolling page, no Next button. Progress is the ring in the header. Room at the bottom for the Ask toolbar.

title: Both swipes.
text: Right = Review (accent). Left = Archive (dark). Both commit, both blur the displaced row.

title: No avatars on list rows.
text: Identity on a row is the author name in its own column. The reader’s avatar lives in the inbox header; the author’s photo on the PR page.

title: Notes about a file look like comments.
text: An AI note on a diff is a comment card by “Pulls”: white, rounded, soft shadow. Not a loose line above the code.

title: Search is a bottom bar on every inbox.
text: Profile at the top, “Search or ask Pulls” floating at the bottom, no search icon in the header.

title: Two accepted row anatomies.
text: Canonical: P’s number column, then the title; author, checks, diffstat, age in fixed columns. Alternative: U’s status circle + number leading the row. Nothing else.

title: One real AI icon.
text: Withdrawn on 2026-10-14: Tavi said the sparkle does not stay, so no icon marks AI. AI actions are marked by their words ("Ask AI", "Analyze") and by the live progress indicator of rule 72. The text it had: an icon from a published set (Lucide sparkles), never a hand-drawn glyph, one per screen.

title: Tabs are an underline, not a box.
text: A hairline under Summary / Description and the accent underline on the active tab. No hairline above.

title: Cites sit on the text line.
text: Same cap height as the body, no vertical padding; tint and a thin border do the “different” work. Never taller than the line, never alone on a line.

title: Air between blocks.
text: A comment card or stats row never touches the diff. At least 24px above the diff’s top edge.

title: Checkboxes are bare.
text: Reviewed is a checkbox and a word. No pill, chip or border around it.

title: Tour position lives in a sticky strip.
text: N of M · title · ring is a sticky strip under the header; it updates as the next section reaches the top. The count exists only there, never inline above a section title.

title: Progress states show the work, not blanks.
text: No shimmer bars standing in for content. The live orb plus the outputs with their state: done, writing, pending.

title: Show states interactively.
text: Once a row is accepted, the next deliverable is a clickable prototype with real transitions: tabs, sheets, swipes, comment reply, the tour scroll.

title: Shadows match the canvas on every floating element.
text:
The header round buttons, the bottom search pill, the comment bar, the Tour card and the Ask bar all carry the canvas shadow (`floatShadow`). A missing or different shadow is a defect, not a nit. It was the most repeated complaint in the walkthrough.

On the phone today the shadows are there but faint and flat: a pale halo spread evenly round the edge, with no visible drop below it. The canvas shadow is faint too (8% ink on the round buttons), but it is pushed 2dp down (`0 2px 10px`), and that offset is what makes a button look lifted. The fix is a drawn shadow with a downward offset like the canvas, not a stronger glow. See Elevation & Depth.

Check: put each floating element beside Row W. Same shadow, with a visible drop below it, or fix it.

title: Blur is part of how things move, in three places.
text:
- Scroll edges: row titles blur as they scroll under the top header and under the bottom bar. Today every scroll edge is a hard cut: rows end in a sharp line under the chip row, text runs up to the bottom pill and stops, and content is sliced under a sheet's fixed header and under the diff's sub-header. The blur belongs at all of them.
- The swiped row blurs as it is displaced, as in the design. This is the same thing as rules 17 and 32. The canvas row moves sideways about 132 to 136dp with a 1.3px blur and a side shadow. Today it slides fully sharp, and the Review action is a flat teal rectangle with square corners and no shadow.
- The scope chips: switching between Waiting on you, Authored and All is liked and keeps its motion. It needs a blur transition, where the outgoing and incoming text overlap. The exact blur is not specified yet. Rule 67 is one possible reference.

title: Build to the canvas measurably. "Different" is a defect.
text:
"Close" is not accepted. What was flagged:

- Spacing inside Inbox rows, horizontal and vertical. The columns are not fixed (rule 13): the gap between the added and removed numbers changes from row to row, and the status marks sit at slightly different positions.
- A divider that the canvas has and the Inbox lacks: a line directly under the project heading. Tours has a hairline under its heading, and the Inbox draws hairlines only above later groups, so the group heading must be treated the same on every tab.
- The bottom search pill sits too low, with its lower edge almost on the system gesture bar. Raise it. The Ask bar on the Tour is in the same low position.
- On the Overview the top part is bigger in the design and is not stuck to the top of the phone.

Check: render the screen and the canvas row at the same size, side by side, before showing it. Measure gaps. Do not eyeball them.

title: Icons: keep the coloured Claude Code and Codex marks, cut the rest.
text:
- Only the Claude Code and Codex marks stay, in colour. Both are monochrome today, a black asterisk and a grey knot.
- The model is shown by its own icon. The Model row in the ⋯ sheet shows a robot head, and should show the icon of the model that was selected.
- No generic AI glyph, no decorative icon. The ones named so far: the robot head (on each Tours row, on the Overview's "Not analyzed yet" card and on the Model row), the sparkle (on "AI Analysis" in Settings and on "Ask AI" in the toolbar over a selected line), the compass (beside "Take a tour of this pull request" and inside the "Give me a tour" button), the chat bubble (in the Ask bar) and the speech bubble on "Request changes". By the same kind: the plug on Server, the layout glyphs on Unified and Split, the zoom magnifiers on Code size, and the globe, key and eye in the Server fields.
- Never the same icon twice on one card. Ask of every icon what fact it carries. This is rule 1 applied to icons.

The robot head also works as a status indicator, because the ring around it turns while a tour is writing. Not complained about: the three icons in the header capsule on the Overview, the gear, and the icons in the profile sheet.

Settled on 2026-10-14: the sparkle does not stay either, so rule 37 is withdrawn and no screen has an AI icon.

The `bans` check counts uses of the robot head, the sparkle, the compass, the chat bubble and the speech bubbles (`ai-glyph`), so new code cannot add one. The count may only fall.

title: One visual dialect: every screen is in the mobile style.
text:
A screen that looks like the old app is a defect. Seen on:

- Settings: font, spacing and pills differ from the rest, and it has the old icons. The sheet is a greyer cream than the Inbox, its close button is a bare ✕, and its segmented controls are the reverse of the Inbox capsule (rule 70). Its model selector must be the mobile one already made. Today it is a cramped dropdown that reads "Default (reco…" with "Default" shown twice.
- The Commands menu: flat rows straight on the cream with no cards, small grey icons, and rows cut by an ellipsis.
- The screen behind the project name: a breadcrumb, bare icons, a bordered filter box and select, and a loading spinner, with none of the round shadowed buttons.
- The file switcher in the Diff: plain grey counts that should be coloured as in the diff, a font that differs from the file name above it, and different files cut to the identical text.
- The toolbar that floats over a selected diff line, with a cut label and the sparkle (rule 48).

Reuse the components already built for mobile (model selector, sheets) instead of rebuilding a web version. The profile sheet is the reference for right.

Check: for every screen reachable from the main flow, ask "does this look like the old app?" before shipping.

title: Never make the reader wait for what the app already knows.
text: Opening a PR shows the title, the number and the rest of the header at once, because they are already loaded. Today a PR opens with "Checks None" and only two tabs, and the Conversation count and the real check state arrive a moment later, so the page fills in piece by piece. Moving between the Overview tabs has no load: content loads as the reader scrolls, the first items appear immediately, and the data is already fetched in the background. Which tab was meant is not named.

title: No loading screens. If something must wait, use skeletons.
text:
This is for page and list content whose shape is known. It does not override rule 43: AI work in progress (Analyzing) still shows the live orb and its outputs, with no shimmer bars.

Today opening a PR puts up an empty page with a spinner and "Loading pull request…", and the project screen does the same, although the title, number and author are already known from the row that was tapped. The Analyzing state puts shimmer bars under each file row, against the wording of rule 43. See the Decision log.

title: Refresh is silent.
text: Pull down must not show a refresh indicator. The app refreshes by itself and does not show it. There is no Refresh button or command anywhere ("we should be refreshing ourselves so there should be no need for the user to refresh"): a pull request takes new commits by itself, and a page reloads quietly when the app comes back to the front. Today the pull-to-refresh spinner is drawn on top of the first row's title, with no space reserved for it.

title: If it looks tappable, it does something.
text: The project heading on Tours looks tappable and does nothing: tapping it lights a grey press highlight across the heading and then nothing opens. It should open the project. On the Overview, the project name at the end of the meta line opens a screen in the old style, so the project destination must be in the new style (rule 49). The author name on the Overview does respond to a tap, which is right, and the branch chip copies the branch name. This is rule 4's "tappable rows look tappable", run the other way.

title: Tabs are easy to hit.
text: The tabs on the Overview are hard to hit. The hit area was not measured. Rule 12 asks for generous element size, and the kit's touch target is 44dp (`TOUCH`). In the frames the tabs are plain text labels with a teal underline under the active one, with no fill or padding, and "Conversation 23" runs close to the right edge.

title: The bottom pill is the one way to find a PR.
text:
- It reads "Search or ask Pulls" as in the design (rule 35). The app shows "Search pull requests" on the Inbox and "Search tours" on Tours. With the keyboard up the pill rides on top of it.
- It takes pasted links and PR numbers as well as text.
- So the "Open pull request" field in the profile sheet goes.

title: Row gestures are the same on Inbox and Tours.
text: Tours rows do nothing when swiped. They get a cancel on one side and open on the other, and tap still opens. This follows rules 15, 17 and 32: one row anatomy, both swipes, blur the displaced row. Today a Tours row is a robot icon in a ring, a one-line title cut with an ellipsis, and "Writing · about a minute" under it.

title: Swiping moves between the Overview tabs.
text: The Overview has three tabs: Summary, Description and Conversation (with a count). The canvas rules name only Summary and Description. Swiping left and right changes between them, with easy, clean swipes. Rule 9 still holds: files in the diff are never switched by horizontal swipe.

title: Sheets with long content pull all the way up.
text: Two bottom sheets cannot be pulled fully up. The ⋯ sheet is cut off at "Close pull request", with Review with AI, Review through a lens, Commands and Refresh below the fold, and the Select model sheet is cut off after Sonnet 5.5. The Ask sheet is nearly full height, so sheets are not all one height. Rule 5 prefers sheets over pages, so a sheet has to behave like a full surface when its content needs it. Sheets at their normal height are fine, the profile sheet included.

title: Menus and sheets open and close with a transition.
text: A menu in the Diff needs an open and a close transition. The menu at that moment is the Aa menu (Smaller, Default, Larger, Wrap long lines, Show review comments, Copy path, Open on GitHub, Load the whole file), not the file switcher. What is wrong with the motion is still Tavi's to say, and a reference showing how those transitions should look is pending. Rule 44 applies once it arrives. Rule 68 applies now: answer at once.

title: A control appears only where it works.
text: The Smaller / Default / Larger menu on the Tour does nothing there, so drop it. The Aa button on the Tour header opens it together with Wrap long lines and Show review comments, which are settings for code, and the Tour has no code on it. The same button on the Diff also holds Copy path, Open on GitHub and Load the whole file, which are fine. Same principle as rule 1: if it does not tell or do anything, cut it.

title: Commands is a designed menu in the app's style, with fewer things in it.
text:
- The current one is in the wrong style. Make a new design in the same style as everything else, and make it nice.
- It may hold too many things. "Review with AI" and "Review through lens" need a decision.
- Tentative, not a rule yet: open it on pull down.
- Open: how Commands relates to rule 29's ⋯ sheet. Today "Commands ›" is a row in the ⋯ sheet and in the profile sheet, and tapping it closes the sheet and opens the palette with the keyboard up. Whether it stays a row in the ⋯ sheet is Tavi's call.

title: Ask never needs Analyze first.
text: Tapping Ask opens the bottom sheet with the chat, and the reader chats straight away. The current screen is not acceptable: it is a title, one grey line reading "Analyze this pull request first, then you can ask about it.", a centred Analyze button, and no composer. Rule 19 makes an unanalysed PR a real state, so Ask has to work in that state.

title: AI actions answer the tap at once and never strand the reader.
text:
Pressing Analyze gave slow feedback. A double tap cancelled the run, and after the cancel there was no way to restart. The card then said "Analyzed" with the Tour step still an empty circle and an italic "Starting Claude…". Nothing said the run was stopped, and the only "Analyze again" was a tile inside the ⋯ sheet.

Checks:

- The first tap shows a response immediately.
- A second tap cannot cancel. Cancelling is a deliberate action.
- A cancelled or failed run always offers a way to start again.
- No state is a dead end.

title: The comment composer is a bar you type into.
text: Tapping a line of the diff opens a comment and in-review control at the bottom that is not liked. Two things appear together: a pill reading "Comment · In review ✕" between a round ‹ button and a round teal › button, and a small white toolbar floating over the selected line (rule 49). The words sit in a pill, so it reads as a label and not as a field you can type in. It used to be a bar you could just type in, which is better, and the buttons can be integrated into it. It is also missing its shadow (rule 45). A few variants are to be tried, so treat the form as open. This is the app-side counterpart of rule 10.

title: Reviewed moves you on.
text: Pressing Reviewed moves to the next file that is not reviewed, and marks the finished file, for example by greying it out a little. Today ticking Reviewed leaves the reader on the same file and shows a toast ("1 of 134 files reviewed") over the bottom of the diff. Back on the Overview the file is struck through and the button says "Review 133 files", so the count of what is left already updates. Rule 41 still holds: Reviewed itself stays a bare checkbox and a word.

title: One destination, one presentation.
text:
The same screen always opens the same way: always as a sheet, or always as a page. In the reference app the sign-in screen is a bottom sheet from one place and a full page from another, which is confusing. This extends rule 5: once a destination is a sheet, every route to it uses the sheet. In this app, check destinations that can be reached from more than one place, such as the model selector (rule 49).

Check: for each screen reachable from two or more places, open it from each. Same presentation every time.

title: A segmented pill moves its highlight, and the new content fades in.
text:
When a pill that switches between modes is tapped, the active highlight slides across to the new segment instead of jumping, and the new content fades in. This is the motion that goes with rule 27. It is one possible reference for the blur transition on the scope chips left open in rule 46, and it is not said to be the one.

Check: tap a segment. The highlight travels to it and the content fades in.

title: Reactive first, springy second.
text:
A control or sheet answers the instant it is touched. A spring or bounce is a bonus, not the requirement. A small bounce that fires the moment a character is typed was liked. This applies to rule 59 (transitions) and rule 63 (AI actions answer at once): sheets, the Analyze tap and the comment bar.

Check: tap or type and note how soon anything visibly changes. A plain transition that starts at once beats a springy one that starts late.

title: Elements that exist in both states keep their position.
text:
When a screen changes state, whatever is present in both states stays exactly where it was, so the change reads as a layer arriving instead of a new screen. In this app the nearest cases are the Overview header across the Tour (rule 23) and the bottom bar across screens.

Check: flip between two states of a screen and watch. Anything that exists in both must not jump.

title: The same control looks the same on a page and in a sheet.
text:
Confirmed by Tavi on 2026-10-14. In the reference app the round ✕ in a sheet is the same white circle with a soft shadow as the round buttons on the page behind it. In this app the Settings sheet had a bare ✕ and segmented controls that were the reverse of the Inbox capsule (rule 49), so one kind of control looked different on a page and in a sheet. Now a sheet's close and back buttons are the round white button with its shadow, and the segmented controls in a sheet are the Inbox capsule. Which way a segmented control goes is still Tavi's call: the canvas capsule is a white track with a grey selected segment, the reference app uses a grey track with a white selected segment, and the app follows the canvas until he says otherwise.

Check: take one kind of control (close button, segmented control, chip, round button). Find it on a page and in a sheet. Same shape, fill and shadow.

title: A live indicator may have shimmer bars under it.
text:
Rule 43 says no shimmer bars standing in for content. Tavi confirmed that bars are fine next to a live indicator, as in Perplexity's "Thinking…", where three grey bars sit under the mark and the word, the second and third a little shorter than the first. So the live indicator stays, and grey bars may sit under it as a hint of where the output will arrive. Bars never replace the indicator and never stand alone. Rule 51's skeletons for pages and lists whose shape is known are unchanged. The canvas text of rule 43 is unchanged.

Check: while AI work runs there is a live indicator on screen. Any bars sit under it.

title: Thinking text is a shimmering plain sentence, each step with its own icon.
text:
Tavi asked for the AI's thinking text to look more like Perplexity's. While work runs there is one line, a present-tense verb and the elapsed seconds ("Working 12s"; "Thinking" before the first step), the verb in the muted colour and the seconds in the faint one, in tabular digits, shimmering together. The shimmer leaves the text at full strength and dims a tilted band to a third of its opacity as it sweeps left to right, 1200ms a pass; with system animations off nothing sweeps. Each step is one plain sentence about the task, never the tool, in regular weight and never italic, after a 16dp icon of what that step does, in the muted colour, in a 28dp column: a page for reading a file, a magnifier for a search, a terminal for a command, a pen for an edit, a light bulb for thinking, a pen on a line for writing, a cog for a status line and a wrench for any other tool. A failed step shows a red ✕ in a circle and a warning an amber refresh, in the same colour as their sentence. This replaces the earlier dot: Tavi asked for "its own specific icon to the left, not a bullet point". The live orb sits under the newest line on the icons' column at 16dp. When the line is replaced by another, the old one leaves upward through a 2px blur while the new one rises in from below, 150ms ease-in-out, 8dp of travel, a 50ms gap (transitions.dev, Thinking states). When work ends the shimmer stops and the line becomes "Worked for 2m 3s", a button with a chevron, right when folded and down when open, whose steps open under it with no line beside them: the icons make the column. The sizes taken from screenshots are estimates, not measured on a device.

Check: start an analysis and watch it. One header line with the time, a dim band passing through it. Each step line has the icon of what it does, and none is italic. When the work ends, the shimmer stops and the line goes to the past tense with a chevron. With animations off nothing sweeps.

title: Motion uses one set of numbers.
text:
Tavi sent transitions.dev as the reference. Durations: 150ms for closes and text swaps, 250ms for opens, tabs and page slides, 350ms for a panel closing, 400ms for a panel opening. One easing, smooth out, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, for opens, closes and slides; ease-in-out for swaps; linear for shimmer. Blur is 2px for small things and 3px for page-sized changes. Scale is 0.97 for menus and 0.96 for dialogs. Travel is 4 to 8dp for text and pages. The mapping from the library's transitions to this app's surfaces was proposed by the rules file and Tavi can retune any row: menus use the dropdown recipe, dialogs the modal one, sheets panel reveal, the capsule tabs sliding, page changes page side-by-side, the thinking line shimmer text and thinking states. Looping effects follow the system setting "Remove animations".

Check: open and close one menu, one sheet, one dialog and one toast. Each takes the time above and eases out.

title: Fixed edges fade. They never cut or smear.
text:
Anything pinned at the edge of something that scrolls has an edge fade on the content that passes under it: the chips and header on Home, a sheet's header, the Tour strip, the bottom search pill. The content goes to the page colour over about 32dp at the top (longer at a tall pill, about 130dp at the bottom of Home) with a blur that grows toward the pinned edge. The blur is made from content that continues past the edge, so a row at the edge is softened and faded, never stretched or sliced. The fade stops at the pinned thing. It never blurs a chip, a button or a header. Nothing white sits behind a floating pill: the rows fade into the page and the pill carries its own shadow.
This is rule 46's first bullet, made exact.

Check: scroll a list slowly and fast under each pinned header and pill. No row ends in a hard line, no text is stretched into blocks, the chips and buttons stay sharp, and nothing white sits under a pill.

title: A group title has one line under it. A heading has none.
text:
A group title in a list (the repository titles in the Inbox) has the single hairline under it that the canvas has (rule 47). It has none above it, so the first title has nothing between it and the chips, and a title never has a line above and below at once. A section heading on a page (Files, What needs a human, Brief) has no line under it in any state of the page.
It replaces the "try a separator under Files" of B3 and B4: nothing is added, and the line under What needs a human goes.

Check: look at every heading on Home, the Overview and the Analyze result. Group titles have one line under them. Headings have none.

title: Dark mode is a neutral grey.
text:
In dark mode every surface is a grey with no colour cast: the red, green and blue values differ by at most 2. The accent stays teal. Values read off Perplexity's dark mode in his recording (frames 05:42 and 06:06): page #161616, raised surfaces and the composer #1D1D1D, chips and the segment track #212121, sheet paper #1B1B1B, border #2B2B2B, text #E3E3E3, muted text #9D9D9D. The light theme is unchanged.

Check: dark mode beside Perplexity's, with the same content. The greys match and nothing looks blue or green.

title: Sheets rest at two heights.
text:
Every sheet rests at its normal height (its content, at most half the screen) or at the tall height near the top, and slides between them. A sheet whose content is short, the profile sheet included, can still be lifted to the tall height: the room under its content is the sheet's paper. A quick throw goes to the next stop, a slow release to the nearest one, a long drag down closes. The grab bar (the lip) at the top is the handle. This holds for every sheet, the profile sheet included. The header is fixed and the content scrolls under it through the edge fade of rule 74, so the ✕ never overlaps text. A sheet with a field (Commands, the chat) opens at its normal height too, with no keyboard ("it goes into this text mode immediately" was jarring). Tapping the field, or lifting the sheet, brings the keyboard up and the sheet to the tall height; lowering it puts the keyboard away.
It replaces the profile sheet's exemption in rule 58, which Tavi gave when he did not yet know he could not pull it up.

Check: open every sheet. It rests at the stop it should and can go to the other one. The header stays put and nothing is sliced under it.

title: A sheet opened from a sheet is a page inside it.
text:
Language from Settings, Select model from the Analyze card, Effort from the model list: the new content slides sideways inside the same sheet. The sheet and its lip stay still, the header stays fixed, the ✕ becomes ←, and back returns to where you were with the scroll position kept. The parent never closes and reopens. This is how Claude's app does it. Switching an engine inside a picker changes its list in place and does not close the sheet.
It makes rule 66 exact for sheets.

Check: open a page inside a sheet and go back. Only the content moved, the sheet did not blink, and the list is where you left it.

title: A sheet's body is its list.
text:
Commits, Files and Checks are plain lists in a sheet, with no panel inside the panel. Rows are bigger (at least 60dp) with whole titles that wrap, as rows are everywhere else. No instruction names a key a phone does not have ("shift-click"). Checks lists failed first, then running, then passed, and a row taps through to the check.

Check: open each of the three sheets. A list on the sheet's own paper, whole titles, rows as big as in the Inbox.

title: A narrowed view always shows the way back.
text:
When a screen shows part of something, such as one commit of six, a bar that stays on screen says so ("Viewing commit 3 of 6") and carries a "Show all" pill. Nobody has to find the way back. The bar is pinned over the Overview and over the Diff, so scrolling never takes it away.

Check: pick one commit. The way to see all changes is visible without scrolling or opening a menu.

title: Settings show what you are choosing.
text:
Where a setting changes how something looks, the control is the thing itself, as a small sample. Diff layout is two small diffs you tap. Code size is three sizes with a line of code under them that resizes. Code font is a list where each font is set in its own face on a sample line. A word or an icon is only for a setting that has no look.

Check: open Settings. Every look-changing setting shows its result without leaving the sheet.

title: Pressing tints. It never moves anything.
text:
A row, a tile, a card or a sheet row tints while it is held and nothing else: no scale, no shift, no growth. Small controls (round buttons, pills, chips, the send circle) may keep their 0.97 press. A tap on a heading that opens nothing does not change colour either.
Which "these" he meant at 27:56 is my reading: he says it right after the Checks and ⋯ sheets, so I took it to be the sheet's rows and tiles.

Check: press and hold a row in each sheet, a card on the Overview and a tile in the ⋯ sheet. Only the tint changes.

title: Edit where it is. Confirm with a toast.
text:
Text you own is edited where it is: tapping the title or description of your own pull request turns it into a field, and leaving it saves. There is no "Edit" button. A control that copies or toggles keeps its face: copying the branch shows a small toast ("Branch name copied") and the pill goes on showing the branch.

Check: tap the title of your own PR. Tap the branch pill. Neither changes what is around it.

title: Send is off until there is something to send.
text:
A send button is grey and does nothing until the field has text.

Check: open every composer empty. The send button is disabled.

title: Skeletons shimmer.
text:
Every skeleton bar carries a shimmer: a soft band, about 40% of the bar's width, sweeps left to right every 1200ms on a linear curve, in light and dark. With the system setting "Remove animations" the bar sits still. A skeleton that does not move is a defect. Under a live indicator the bars of rule 71 do the same.

Check: put each skeleton on screen for three seconds. The light visibly passes through it.

title: A card that works keeps its height.
text:
Nothing on a page moves while AI works. The Analyze card is one fixed height (72dp) in every state: idle, running and finished. Its status is one line that ends in an ellipsis, because this is not important content and tapping it shows more. The step chips are not in the card while it runs, and the log opens in a sheet. A new line or a wrapped chip never moves what is below.

Check: run an analysis and watch the page. Nothing above or below the card moves.

title: One job, one control.
text:
Stop is the orb: tapping where the orb is stops the run, and there is no second Stop pill or second icon. A repeat action is the try-again arrow with an accessibility label, not the word Redo. A control that explains itself in a line of its own ("The Analyze button runs the last choice") goes, which is rule 1.
Rule 63 holds: a second quick tap never cancels.

Check: look at the Analyzing card and the result. Each job has one control.

title: Pages slide. They never pop.
text:
Opening a PR from a row, going between Overview tabs and returning all slide the new page in from the side it belongs to, with the numbers of rule 73 for "page side by side" (250ms, 8dp, a fade, 3px of blur). Swiping between Summary and Description moves the whole section with the finger, as a page. Opening from a swiped row uses the same slide as opening by a tap.
It extends rule 57.

Check: open a PR from a row by tap and by swipe, then swipe between tabs. A slide every time and the section follows the finger.

title: A picker shows the short list first.
text:
A list of models or engines shows the few most people want, newest first, and puts the rest below the Effort row under a small "Older models" heading, in a card of their own that is always there to scroll to, never folded (Claude's picker lists them the same way, under "Other models"; he called a fold inside the list "not how it looked in the video"). A row is a name only, with no ID line and no description unless the name alone is not enough. The recommended choice carries a "Recommended" pill (26dp tall, 13sp medium, a neutral grey with dark text, as Claude's is; the teal wash was "the wrong color") and the selected one a plain, larger ✓, never the word "Default" beside a check. The footnote under a list is tiny, as in Claude's (13sp, the one place that goes below rule 14's floor, because he asked for it). There is no custom model ID field. "Newest first" is read from the version in the name: the newest version of each family (Opus, Sonnet, Fable, GPT) from the newest generation, the default and any alias such as "Opus (1M context)"; every other version goes below the Effort row. The model in use is never hidden: it is in one list or the other. A Codex name loses the hyphens between its words ("GPT-5.1 Codex Max"). Claude Code lists its models by family alone ("Opus"), with the version only in the description, so the row takes the version from there ("Opus 5.5") and sorts by it. Claude Code's recommended effort is the CLI's own default for that model, and the Effort row names the level that will run.
F34 stays: tapping Quick, Standard or Deep on the Analyze sheet starts the analysis. (The first digest read this as choosing a model. The recording at 13:17 to 13:41 shows him tapping a preset, finding it started at once, and calling it awesome. Choosing a model only saves it.)

Check: open the model sheet for each engine beside Claude's. The same shape.

title: A path is cut from the left.
text:
A path shows its end, because the end is what tells files apart: "…/domains/practice/components". Folders are dropped from the front whole, never cut in the middle of a name. Tapping the path line shows the whole path. The file name comes first. People's names and titles wrap whole (rule 2) and are not cut with an ellipsis.

Check: put a long path on a file row and in the diff header. The end of the path is readable, the whole path is one tap away and no name is cut.

title: Long threads fold.
text:
Each comment in Conversation folds. A folded comment is the name, the age and a chevron on one line, with its first line dimmed under it. The first comment starts open. Bot comments, such as CodeRabbit's, start folded. "commented" is never written, because it can only be a comment. The age and the chevron sit at the right edge of every header, so they line up from one comment to the next whatever the length of the name, and a long name wraps onto a second line rather than push them or be cut ("align these always").
Pushed commits are not in the Conversation. They have a tab of their own, Commits, between Summary and Conversation ("Commits should be somewhere else. Maybe a tab"). It lists them oldest first and says so at the top, numbers each one, gives every row room (14dp above and below, a hairline between), and keeps "All commits" as the first row. A tap shows only that commit, a long-press stretches the range from the last one tapped, and the banner of rule 80 says what is shown. The Commits cell on the page opens this tab. Commits GitHub did not send are named in one row that opens them on GitHub. The tabs carry no counts, so they fit a phone: they spread from the first label at the start to the last at the end with even gaps, and when they cannot fit they scroll sideways instead of cutting a label.

Check: open a Conversation with ten comments. Every one folds and unfolds, none says "commented", the ages are in one column, and no commit is in it. Open Commits: the order is written, every commit has its number.

title: The top of a code screen is short. The code gets the screen.
text:
The header of the Diff is the back button and the capsule, nothing else. The file's name sits at the bottom between the ‹ › buttons ("put it between the arrows"), centred in a round pill, in the face it has on the file rows (the code font would break a long name), whole, on up to three lines; under a short name the end of its folder (rule 90) and "3 of 12". A tap on it opens the Files sheet, the one place a file is picked (rule 101). The note about the file and the line with its counts and the Reviewed box are part of the scrolling content and scroll away with the code, so pinned chrome is no more than a fifth of the screen. The file ends where the code ends: nothing scrolls into empty space, only room to clear the bar.

Check: open a file with a long path and a long note. Pinned chrome is no more than a fifth of the screen. The name is whole at the bottom between the arrows. Scroll to the end: the last line is the last thing.

title: Swiping the diff goes to the next file. The header never shifts.
text:
A swipe left or right on the code goes to the next or previous file, like the ‹ › buttons, and the page follows the finger. This reverses the "never switched by horizontal swipe" half of rule 9, as he asked. On code wider than the screen a swipe first scrolls the code, and changes file only once the code is at its edge; on wrapped code, and anywhere off the code (the note, the counts line, a thread card), it changes file at once. Two fingers pinch, a held finger selects, and nothing changes file while lines are selected. From the last file, a swipe left continues to the Tour; from the first, a swipe right goes back to the Overview. The capsule keeps its shape on the Diff, the Overview and the Tour: three view icons and one corner slot, which is ⋯ on the Overview and the Tour and Aa on the Diff. Swiping between the three never moves the header: the back button, the capsule and the bar of rule 80 are drawn once over all three pages, so only what is under them changes, and the selected segment of the capsule slides to its new place. From the Tour a swipe right goes back to the Diff, and from the Overview's last tab a swipe left goes on to the Diff. A pinch scales the code under the fingers and pans with them; when they lift, the new size is kept and the line that was under them stays there.
Aa opens "Text and tools" as a bottom sheet, and every choice in it shows what it does instead of describing it ("why am I not seeing what these do"): the layout first, as the two small diffs of rule 81 (Split only on a screen 640dp or wider; on a phone it is shown dim with "wider screens"), the code size capsule over a sample that resizes and shows wrapping, the code font as a page inside the sheet, wrap long lines and review comments as switches, then the file's own actions (copy the path, open it on GitHub, load the whole file) and one row to the pull request's ⋯ actions.

Check: swipe between files and between views. The header is the same pixels throughout. Swipe on code wider than the screen: it scrolls first. Open Aa: the diff layout is the first thing, and every choice changes a sample in front of you.

title: One way to start a comment, one sheet to write it in.
text:
The only way in is selecting lines: a tap on a line number, extended by dragging down the gutter. There is no toolbar floating over the selected lines. Selecting lines turns the bar at the bottom into the comment bar: a ✕ to let the lines go, the field (its placeholder is the one place the range is written, "Comment on lines 356–358"), a small toggle for "In review" or "Post now", a ⋯ and the send button; letting the lines go turns it back into ‹ name ›. The ⋯ opens a small sheet: Ask about these lines (the Ask sheet, with the lines attached as a card), Copy file and lines, Copy GitHub link. Someone who cannot comment gets the ✕, the range and the ⋯. A comment thread under the line stays a card in the code (rule 9); an Ask about lines shows under them as the chat shows it, the question in its bubble and the answer as plain text with no box (rule 99). Nothing repeats what is already on screen. Tapping a file note opens Ask with that note attached as a card above the field, which a ✕ leaves out.
This replaces rule 64's "a bar you type into" and the toolbar of rule 49. He chose option B of the target designs, the bar ("I'll live with this option for now"), over the sheet of option A ("I hate this so much").

Check: comment on three lines. One bar, one field, and nothing on the screen says the same thing twice. Let the lines go: the file name is back.

title: Code, flows and tables in AI text work like the diff.
text:
A code block in a tour or an answer is the diff's code view: syntax colours, sideways scroll, pinch zoom. A flow is drawn by the app from structured data, never printed as text. A table keeps a readable width for each column (the description never below about 230dp) and scrolls sideways with a fade at its edge. Inline code shows as code and never with its backticks. Pseudocode is coloured like code, from the same palette. A call tree and a file tree are drawn as trees with guide lines, and a file in a tree that the pull request changes opens it. A flow line that does not parse stays as words in its place while the rest of the flow is drawn. In a tour's "In the code" list the place sits on its own line and its reason under it at the full width, so a long file name never squeezes the reason into a narrow column (24:30 in the second walkthrough).

Check: open a tour with a code block, a flow and a table. The code scrolls and zooms, the flow is drawn, no column is squeezed to four characters.

title: What the AI mentions is a link.
text:
Every mention of a file, line, symbol or dimension, in a note, the summary, a finding, a tour or an answer, is a link that scrolls to that place. Cites are teal text with no underline. They look like what they are and sit on the text line (rule 39). A file name or `path:line` in backticks is a link when it names a changed file, and a mention of a file the pull request does not change opens it on GitHub. What is posted to GitHub links each cite to the file at the head commit.
He called F43 "super, super, super important", so the analysis, tour, Ask and review instructions all say it and a check makes sure.

Check: tap every cite in an analysis, a file note, a finding and an answer on lines. Each scrolls to its place.

title: The Tour strip is calm.
text:
The strip is one line under the header: a ring, the title and a chevron, each in its own column so the text never runs under the ring. The title is one line with an ellipsis or two whole lines, never cut in half. The ring fills continuously with the tour's scroll position, not in jumps. "2 of 4" is not shown (rule 11). The chevron opens the sections as a bottom sheet with the read ones ticked. When the tour ends there is no "Back to the pull request" button: the header or a swipe leaves it. The strip takes the edge fade of rule 74.

Check: scroll a tour slowly. The ring fills as you go, the title is whole, and the last screen has no button.

title: No machinery on content screens.
text:
A tour or a note does not show the model name, token counts or cache numbers. They live in Settings and the model sheet. Rewrite is an icon at the card's corner with no word.

Check: search each AI screen for a model name or a token count. None, except in the pickers.

title: Ask replies are plain text.
text:
The AI's reply has no box, fill or shadow. Only your own message is a bubble, in the accent colour. There is never a bubble with dots in it. "Clear" is not a word on the screen: a new-chat button sits at the top right. Under each answer, sources are chips that scroll to the place, and two or three follow-up questions that tap to send, written each turn by a small fast model. The thinking streams as it happens (rule 72): while a step thinks, its newest two or three lines show under it in the muted colour and fold away when it ends, and the answer appears in its place as it is written, with no jump when the saved reply takes over. The source chips cover the files it read as well as the places it names. The ⋯ menu of Perplexity is not copied.

Check: ask a question. A plain reply, source chips, follow-ups, no dots bubble and no "Clear".

title: No link-out icons.
text:
The app never shows an arrow leaving a box, or any other "opens elsewhere" mark ("never this kind of icon. We're not a web app. We don't open links, not like this"). A row that goes to GitHub carries GitHub's own mark, and any other row says in words what it does.

Check: open every sheet and list. No arrow-out icon anywhere.

title: A long list can be searched, and its sections fold.
text:
A list that can run long (the files, the repositories) has a search field at the top of its sheet (`SheetSearch`: 48dp, the card radius, the float shadow, ✕ to clear), and a row matches when every word typed is in it. The files are one sheet, opened from the Files cell on the Overview and from the file name in the Diff, with the file on screen marked. Sections of files fold under their headings, on the Overview and in the sheet, and a fold is kept while the pull request is open. A pull request with more than 80 files opens with every section folded (in the sheet, the section holding the file on screen stays open), so 80,000 changed lines start as a short list of headings, and the sheet shows the first 300 rows with a row to show all of them. A search opens every section it finds something in.

Check: open a pull request of a few hundred files. Headings first, each opens and folds, the search finds a file by two words of its path, and nothing stutters.

title: A file row swipes like a pull request row.
text:
A file row on the Overview takes the gestures of the Inbox rows (rule 56): a swipe right opens it, as it opens a pull request row, a swipe left marks it reviewed (or not reviewed), a tap opens it and a long-press opens its actions (open, mark reviewed, copy the path, ask about the file). The checkbox sits on the first line of text. The file name comes first, its folder under it cut from the front (rule 90), the counts at the right, and the AI's note in two lines at most.

Check: swipe a file both ways, tap it and hold it. The swipe blurs the row like the Inbox's, and the box lines up with the name.

title: Searching dims what is behind.
text:
While the search on Home waits for its first letter with the keyboard up, the Inbox behind it dims a little (half the sheet's scrim), and a tap on it puts the keyboard away. Once something is typed, the matches are what the search is for, so they are shown at full strength and take taps.

Check: tap the search pill. The list dims. Type a letter: the matches are bright and open with one tap.

title: A new version must be installed, and its changelog is the screen that asks.
text:
When the server has a newer build, Pulls shows only the update screen, from the first frame of a start: "Pulls 0.28.0 is ready", "Update to keep using Pulls.", then every version it brings over the installed one, each with its summary and bullets, and "Update to 0.28.0" as the dark main action at the foot. Nothing closes it but the update; Back leaves the app. Update downloads and installs in the app and says how far it got (a ring while it downloads, the orb while the system installs), and a failed download or install offers Try again rather than letting the reader through. The phone remembers the last offer, so the screen is there before the server answers again, and it goes when the server has nothing newer. Commands has Update Pulls, which asks the server at once and starts the update, or says this is the newest version, and What's new. The phone is also told in a notification when the app is closed. What's new opens by itself once after an install the update screen did not show. The words come from `android/CHANGELOG.md`, written for the reader, not from commit messages.

Check: publish a build with a higher version and open Pulls. The update screen lists what changed and nothing gets past it; Update installs it. Run Update Pulls from Commands with no newer build: it says this is the newest.

title: Motion goes the way you went.
text:
Tavi: "Most transition animations don't seem to naturally follow the movement you're doing. For instance, when I swipe in the PR home to move between the tabs, the direction of the transition does not go into the tab we're going to." Everything moves the way the person moved it. A thing dragged by a finger follows the finger, and when the finger lets go it either settles back where it was or carries on the way the finger went; it never springs back toward the finger's start before going on. The next tab, file, view or page comes in from the right and the one left behind leaves to the left; the previous one comes from the left. Pages sit where the controls show them: tabs in their order, the review's views in the capsule's order (Overview, Changes, Tour), the stack of pages by depth. Back always goes backward, whichever view or page it lands on. A back swipe moves the page with the finger and then carries it on that way, so a swipe from the right edge sends it left. The tab underline and the capsule's pill slide to the new place, and the underline leans toward the next tab while the finger drags. A label that names where you are (the file between ‹ and ›, the Tour's stop) changes the same way: the next file from the right, the next stop rising from below. Commands, pulled down from the Inbox, is a sheet like any other and rises from the bottom (H6); a sheet thrown down carries on down. Nothing that belongs to a page pops while the page slides: it slides with it. A quick throw of 500dp/s counts as a swipe however short it is, and a throw back against the drag cancels it.

Check: on the Overview drag between tabs slowly and let go short, then far, then throw: the rows and the underline go toward the tab you went to, or back where they were, never the other way first. Swipe between files and past the last one, use ‹ ›, the capsule and Back, back-swipe from each edge, pull Commands down and close it.

title: The web looks like the phone.
text:
Tavi: "Let's also have an agent that updates the web page, and makes it like the mobile app looks-wise. The more code we can deduplicate, especially styling-wise, the better." The web app is the same product as the phone app and wears the same look: warm paper, deep teal ink, one teal accent, Geist, the prototype's icons, and the same pills, cards, chips, tabs, sheets and shadows. Neither side has a look of its own. The web takes its tokens from this file's front matter, its icons from `Lu` and its fonts from `PullsFonts` (written into `packages/app/src/design` as generated files), and the phone takes its strings from the web's locale files. A colour, size, radius, shadow, icon or string is added once, at its source, and `pnpm run android:design:update` carries it to the other side. The web may lay a screen out wider, with a side list next to the content from 768px up, but every piece it is made of is the phone's piece.

Check: open the same pull request on the phone and on the web at 390 by 844, in light and dark. Same colours, type, icons, corners and shadows.

title: Pages that sit side by side slide whole.
text:
Tavi, on Inbox and Tours: "It should move like screens side by side", as Grok's Ask, Imagine and Build do, and on Summary and Commits: "pages next to each other just slide, no fade." Screens that sit beside each other (the Inbox and Tours, a repository's pull requests and its tours, the Overview's tabs, the Diff's files) move the whole width of the screen with a gap between them, and nothing fades or blurs. The Inbox and Tours follow a drag anywhere a row does not take it, and settle on the nearer screen or go on the way a throw went (`SidePages`). The Overview's rows and the Diff's file leave the whole width gathering speed and the next arrives from the other edge (`rememberPageSlide(..., full = true)`). A sheet's own pages (Settings to What's new, Code font, Language) travel a third of the sheet's width in 350ms and blur, so the way they go is plain (H1, H4). Only the content under the Overview's tabs swipes between them: a sideways drag on the title, the branch or the numbers does nothing (H32).

Check: tap Tours and drag back to the Inbox from the chips; swipe Summary to Commits and back; open Settings, go to What's new and back. The screens move whole, nothing fades, and Back goes right.

title: Sheets rise from the bottom, bounce a little, and close only when pulled.
text:
Every sheet, Commands included, comes up from the bottom and settles on a spring that goes a little past its place and comes back (H3, H6). Scrolling a sheet's content down and back up never moves the sheet: only a drag that starts with the content at its top, or on the grabber and header, pulls it down (H2).

Check: open Settings, scroll the content down and back up fast: the sheet stays. Pull it down from the header: it follows and closes. Pull the Inbox down for Commands: it rises from the bottom.

title: Taps, swipes and outcomes are felt.
text:
Tavi: "use Android vibrations much more." Every control that plays a cue also vibrates, with the phone's own short effects: a tick for a quiet button or a choice, a click for a main button or a switch, two for a success and a heavy one for a failure. A swipe ticks when letting go would act and again if the finger takes it back, as do Pull for commands and a page that changes under the finger; holding a row is a heavy click. Vibration follows the phone's touch feedback setting and has its own switch under Settings, Sounds.

Check: with Vibration on, tap a tab, swipe a row past its point and back, pull for commands, hold a row, switch the theme. Each is felt; with the switch off none is.

title: Editing looks like editing.
text:
Tapping the title puts the caret where the finger landed, not before the first letter (H34). While the title is edited it is underlined in the accent and the rest of the page fades to a quarter, so it is plain that the page is now about the field (H35); the description's field fades the page around it the same way. Leaving the field brings the page back.

Check: tap in the middle of a pull request's title: the caret is there, the page behind fades, and tapping the empty page saves and brings it back.

title: Names stay on one line.
text:
An author's name, a branch and a tour's author never wrap and never stack a letter to a line (H15, H28). In a row the name takes one line and gives way only at its end. The branch row is always one line: a long branch runs past the edge and the row scrolls sideways to read it all, and "…" is the last resort (H31). A pull request in a stack shows where it sits, "2/10" with the layers mark, under its number, not beside the name (H16). A finished tour's ring is a filled tick and nothing says "Read" (H27).

Check: open the Inbox with a stacked pull request by a long login, and an Overview with a long branch: names are one line, the branch scrolls, and the stack place is under the number.

title: Light and dark wipe in from a corner.
text:
Switching Light and Dark (Settings, or Commands) spreads the new look in a circle from the top corner on the side of the chosen option over the old one, in 650ms, across the page and any sheet over it (`ThemeWipe`). Without system animations the theme simply changes.

Check: in Settings tap Dark, then Light: the new look grows from the top right, then from the top left.
